speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with painful urination. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any rash on your skin or redness on your eyes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome) secondary to an untreated urethritis.

The combination of urethritis (painful urination), asymmetric oligoarthritis (swollen left ankle, now right knee), and recent sexual activity is highly suggestive of this condition. I will now request specific test results to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Syphilis Serology, and HLA-B27 genetic testing.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right Knee X-Ray and Right Knee MRI.
